items.followUp: What are chlorophyll pigments, and what role do they play in photosynthesis?

rubric.why: Identifies pigments by their light-absorbing property.
rubric.description: States that pigments absorb light.
rubric.how: Award for saying pigments absorb light energy or particular wavelengths of light.

rubric.why: Adds the characteristic that pigments are coloured substances or that they give colour.
rubric.description: Identifies pigments as coloured substances or explains their role in colour.
rubric.how: Award for describing pigments as coloured substances, or stating that they reflect light that gives them their colour.

modelAnswer: Pigments are coloured substances that absorb light of particular wavelengths.
They may reflect light of other wavelengths, giving them their characteristic colour.

items.followUp: What is the optimum pH for an enzyme?

rubric.why: Defines optimum temperature by enzyme activity.
rubric.description: States that it is the temperature at which an enzyme works best.
rubric.how: Award for identifying maximum enzyme activity or reaction rate.

rubric.why: Specifies that the optimum is a temperature.
rubric.description: Makes clear that the condition is a temperature.
rubric.how: Award when the answer identifies a temperature at which the stated maximum activity occurs.

modelAnswer: Optimum temperature is the temperature at which an enzyme shows its maximum activity.
At this temperature, the enzyme-catalysed reaction proceeds at its highest rate.

items.followUp: Explain how sugars move from a source to a sink in a plant.

rubric.why: Defines the source in relation to sugar supply.
rubric.description: Explains that a source produces or supplies sugars.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a source, such as a photosynthesising leaf, produces or releases sugars for transport.

rubric.why: Defines the sink in relation to sugar use or storage.
rubric.description: Explains that a sink uses or stores sugars.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a sink uses sugars for growth or stores them.

modelAnswer: A source is a plant part, usually a photosynthesising leaf, that produces and supplies sugars.
A sink is a plant part that uses sugars for growth or stores them.

items.followUp: Give one structural difference between arteries and veins.

rubric.why: Identifies the thicker, more muscular and elastic walls of arteries.
rubric.description: Compares the walls of arteries and veins.
rubric.how: Award for stating that arteries have thicker, more muscular or more elastic walls than veins.

rubric.why: Identifies a defining feature of arteries that distinguishes them from veins.
rubric.description: States the direction of blood flow or the pressure difference.
rubric.how: Award for stating that arteries carry blood away from the heart or that blood in them is under higher pressure.

modelAnswer: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, whereas veins carry blood towards the heart.
Arteries have thick, muscular, elastic walls to withstand high pressure; veins have thinner walls and usually contain valves to prevent backflow.

items.followUp: Name two fields of work related to biology and describe what workers do in each.

rubric.why: Gives a biological profession and explains its work.
rubric.description: Explains medicine as a career.
rubric.how: Award for stating that medical professionals diagnose, prevent or treat disease.

rubric.why: Gives a biological profession and explains its work.
rubric.description: Explains agriculture as a career.
rubric.how: Award for stating that agricultural professionals improve crop production or grow crops.

rubric.why: Gives a biological profession and explains its work.
rubric.description: Explains animal husbandry or veterinary work as a career.
rubric.how: Award for stating that these professionals care for, breed or improve animals or livestock.

rubric.why: Gives a biological profession and explains its work.
rubric.description: Explains fisheries as a career.
rubric.how: Award for stating that fisheries professionals breed, raise, manage or harvest fish.

rubric.why: Gives a biological profession and explains its work.
rubric.description: Explains forestry as a career.
rubric.how: Award for stating that forestry professionals manage, protect or conserve forests and trees.

modelAnswer: Medicine: Medical professionals use biological knowledge to diagnose, prevent and treat diseases.
Agriculture: Agricultural professionals apply biology to grow crops and improve their yield.
Animal husbandry: These professionals breed, care for and improve livestock.
Fisheries: Fisheries professionals breed, raise and manage fish and other aquatic resources.
Forestry: Foresters manage and conserve forests and their plant and animal life.

items.followUp: Describe how the inner membrane of a mitochondrion is adapted for ATP production.

rubric.why: Recognises the mitochondrion's basic outline and enclosing membranes.
rubric.description: Shows the outer boundary and double-membrane structure.
rubric.how: Award for a labelled outer membrane and indication of a double membrane.

rubric.why: Identifies the folded inner membrane.
rubric.description: Shows and labels the inner membrane and cristae.
rubric.how: Award for correctly showing or labelling the inner membrane folds as cristae.

rubric.why: Identifies the internal matrix.
rubric.description: Shows and labels the matrix.
rubric.how: Award for correctly labelling the space enclosed by the inner membrane as the matrix.

rubric.why: States the main function of mitochondria.
rubric.description: Explains that mitochondria produce ATP during cellular respiration.
rubric.how: Award for linking cellular respiration in mitochondria with ATP production or energy supply.

modelAnswer: Draw a simple oval outline for the mitochondrion; the diagram is schematic and not to scale.
Draw and label the outer membrane, then draw the folded inner membrane inside it; label the folds cristae.
Label the compartment enclosed by the inner membrane as the matrix.
Mitochondria are the site of cellular respiration and produce ATP, supplying usable energy to the cell.

items.followUp: What is one way biodiversity helps maintain the stability of an ecosystem?

rubric.why: Defines biodiversity as biological variety.
rubric.description: Defines biodiversity as the variety of living organisms.
rubric.how: Award for referring to variety among organisms, species or living things.

rubric.why: Identifies the role of biodiversity in maintaining ecosystem balance.
rubric.description: Explains its importance for ecosystem stability.
rubric.how: Award for stating that biodiversity helps maintain ecological balance or stable ecosystems.

rubric.why: Identifies resources and products provided by biodiversity.
rubric.description: Explains its value as a source of useful resources.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning food, medicines, fuel, fibres or other useful biological products.

rubric.why: Identifies an important ecological service.
rubric.description: Gives an ecosystem service supported by biodiversity.
rubric.how: Award for a valid service such as pollination, soil formation or fertility, water purification or air purification.

rubric.why: Recognises the conservation and future value of biodiversity.
rubric.description: Explains its importance for conservation or future needs.
rubric.how: Award for stating that biodiversity preserves species or genetic resources for future generations.

modelAnswer: Biodiversity is the variety of living organisms found in an area or on Earth.
It helps maintain ecological balance and stable ecosystems.
It provides useful resources such as food, medicines, fuel and fibres.
Biodiversity supports essential services such as pollination, soil fertility and water purification.
Its conservation protects species and genetic resources for present and future generations.

items.followUp: How is ATP formed from ADP in a cell?

rubric.why: Identifies ATP by its full name or components.
rubric.description: Gives the full name of ATP or identifies its components.
rubric.how: Award for stating that ATP is adenosine triphosphate, made of adenine, ribose and three phosphate groups.

rubric.why: Explains the energy association of ATP's phosphate groups.
rubric.description: States that energy is associated with the bond to the terminal phosphate group.
rubric.how: Award for linking energy release to breaking the bond with the terminal phosphate group.

rubric.why: Shows the reversible ATP–ADP energy cycle.
rubric.description: Explains that ATP can be converted to ADP and phosphate, releasing energy.
rubric.how: Award for stating that ATP loses a phosphate to form ADP and inorganic phosphate.

rubric.why: Explains why ATP is called the cell's energy currency.
rubric.description: States that ATP transfers usable energy for cellular activities.
rubric.how: Award for saying ATP stores or transfers energy and supplies it for cell processes.

modelAnswer: ATP stands for adenosine triphosphate and consists of adenine, ribose and three phosphate groups.
Energy is stored in the bond to its terminal phosphate group.
When this bond is broken, ATP becomes ADP and inorganic phosphate, releasing energy.
ATP transfers this usable energy to cellular processes, so it is called the cell's energy currency.
